applies_why: The judge text uses the absence of a verse whose own words state the contrary as decisive against a point that was answered by cited chain verses, which is what K-C governs.
quote: D1 vs C3 (Matthew 1:16): UNDERDETERMINED -- the passive egennēthē states no verdict on the begetter in either direction, and the defender answered Luke 1:27, Luke 2:4 and Numbers 1:2 in [CR2] section A.3 and [CR3]; the verb change is real [L1]/[L2] but neither text's own words state the other reading's contrary.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires: I weighed reading this as merely descriptive against reading it as forbidding the judge's use of no-explicit-contrary as decisive here.
why: The judge marks the point UNDERDETERMINED because neither text's own words state the other reading's contrary, which is the retired stating-verse test K-C forbids at the judge's seat.
